_comment: Phase B (verification-suite v3.3.0) MCP server registry. bd-mcp (J29) is the Beads task-tracker surface; code-graph-mcp (verification-suite Phase B) is the tree-sitter + SQLite code-graph server. code-graph replaces code-context-mcp, which was removed in 3.3.0 — the stable surface (code_search / code_context / code_index_health) is byte-compatible on inputs and on the documented output fields, and the impact-analysis tools (symbol_callers / impact_of / dead_code / dependency_path) are new with this server. The _phase7_codebase_graph_target placeholder is gone now that it is filled. Variable form is `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.}` because Claude Code sets CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in the spawned MCP server's environment, not in its own — so a bare `${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}` in this project-scoped .mcp.json is unresolved at substitution time and produces an MCP-diagnostics warning. The `:-` default form is the documented fix (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp); .claude-plugin/plugin.json keeps the bare `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` form because the plugin scope substitutes those variables directly. bd's own env sets BD_CWD explicitly (claude-workflow-plugin-j7kk, 39cy): exec-bd.js's resolveBdCwd() precedence is opts.cwd > BD_CWD > CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR > process.cwd(), and bd-mcp/README.md's own env table calls CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR only 'usually' set by Claude Code for a spawned server — an MCP server that launches outside the project root would otherwise walk up to 8 directories from an unrelated cwd looking for .beads/ and can silently resolve the WRONG store or none at all, losing its entire task surface with no error. Setting BD_CWD directly, using the SAME ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-.} substitution already proven reliable for args above, removes the dependency on CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR also being visible inside the spawned process's own environment. CONSIDERED AND REJECTED for this slot: BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 — the incident that raised this rider (task 39cy) also observed bd-mcp going entirely dark under an active schema-version mismatch, and bd itself accepts that flag as an env var (confirmed in its own binary strings). But 39cy's own resolution explicitly treats needing that bypass as a regression to stop and report, not a standing condition to paper over, and bd's own message admits the bypass degrades rather than restores correctness ('queries touching newer schema may fail') — baking it in permanently would convert a loud, unambiguous refusal into a silent, partial one on any FUTURE drift, which is the opposite of this task's own direction. The doctor's bd-version-vs-schema pin (workflow-doctor.sh) is what should catch a recurrence, loudly; this env key stays scoped to store-path resolution, which has no such downside.
